C-001.statement: An entity styling itself the 'State of LOC Nation Global Public Benefit Corporation' (SOLNGPBC), described in its own filings as an 'Established sovereign govt: drafting formal constitution, laws, negotiating treaties', filed fifteen Lobbying Disclosure Act records in 2024-2025 reporting $20 million per quarter — claiming $180 million in lobbying income across nine 2025 filings — through a Delaware-registered shell called LOC COMMUNITY ASSOCIATION whose sole disclosed lobbyist is Rev. Dr. Christina Loren Clement, identified across the filings as 'President of Black USA', '2024 Presidential candidate (assumed the Presidency)', and 'HH Empress Queen'. Detector D9 (shell-pattern scan over all 418K filings) confirms this is a unique-pattern outlier: the next-highest-scoring registrant scores 1 of 6 signals (vs. LOC's 4), and the closest comparable filing in the corpus is THEYFEARTRUTH FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OF AMERICA (zero income, but same self-styled-sovereign category).
limitations: $180M is the sum of all 2025 filings as filed; multiple Q2 2025 amendments at $20M each likely double-count. The deduplicated quarterly figure is $20M × 4 = $80M. OpenLobby reports 14 filings totaling $160M — a small documentation-rule difference at the amendment-counting layer. We report both.

The filer's own disclosure body, per the adversarial fact-checker, states: 'the $20M is pending HR 40 research reimbursement owed to SoLN GPBC entities. It remains unpaid due to federal non-response and is used for reporting and documentation purposes only. It is not a federal payment unless and until processed by the responsible agency.' So Christina Clement is not claiming receipt of $20M from lobbying clients — she is using the LDA income field to register a putative reparations-reimbursement claim against the federal government. The finding stands as 'fictitious filings in the federal lobbying database', but the framing should not over-imply that anyone has paid the $20M.

C-002.statement: Anchor & Arrow Strategies / Anchor & Arrow LLC, founded by former House Armed Services Committee, Sen. Tom Cotton's national-security desk, and Navy/Marine Corps appropriations staff, registered 13 AI- and autonomous-defense startups as lobbying clients in 2024-2026 (102 filings, $2.41M lobbying revenue). USAspending.gov data confirms at least four of those clients received material DoD contracts during the same period — Apex Technology ($25.7M, including a $22M Air Force SBIR Phase II STRATFI for multi-mission satellites awarded after Anchor & Arrow's Q3 2025 registration), Overland AI ($8.86M across seven SBIR awards), Base Operations ($1.32M for AI-driven security intelligence), and Gallatin AI ($150K SBIR Phase I).

Independent biographical verification (Noonan)
Independent biographical verification (Zumbar)

limitations: Revolving-door + lobbying-followed-by-contract patterns alone are not illegal; SBIR awards are competitively reviewed and typically span multi-year decision cycles.

USAspending.gov search did not return matches for Palantir, Saronic, Epirus, CX2, American Phalanx — these companies may have prime-contract awards under slightly-different recipient names or under classified award streams (USAspending does not capture classified obligations).

C-003.statement: Across the 2024-2026 Senate LDA filings, 743 distinct registrants disclose foreign_entities[]; only 61 (8%) also appear in the U.S. DOJ FARA registrant list — a 682-name aggregate 'FARA gap'. Detector D10 narrows this gap to 200 specific filings that combine the gap with at least one of (a) non-US client country, (b) foreign-government-policy lobbying topics (embassy/ambassador/sanctions/FARA mentions), or (c) state-owned-enterprise client naming (Republic of, Kingdom of, Ministry of, etc.). The narrowed list surfaces concrete candidates including Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld lobbying for Ant Group Co. (China), Rich Feuer Anderson lobbying for Ant Group Co. (China), Bracewell LLP lobbying for Tele-Fonika Cable Americas, and FGS Global lobbying for Wuxi Biologics USA LLC (HK).

external_sources.purpose: FARA bulk source (DOJ-mirrored XML)

limitations: FARA and LDA capture overlapping but distinct activity. Many gap filings are legitimate (US client owned by a foreign parent does not by itself require FARA from its lobbyist).
Name match used uppercased equality. Some gap entries (e.g., Akin Gump) likely DO have FARA registrations under specific lawyers, not the firm name.

C-004.statement: A multi-hop revolving-door detector (D11) — joining lobbyists whose covered_position text names a specific committee, current quarterly filings, and the issue-code those filings lobby on — surfaces a particularly dense cluster at Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck LLP: Russell Sullivan (former Staff Director, Senate Finance Committee) and Mark Warren (former Chief Tax Counsel, Senate Finance Committee; Senior Tax Counsel to Sen. Thune; Tax Counsel, House Ways & Means; Deputy Assistant Secretary, Treasury Legislative Affairs) both lobby Apollo Global Management, Athene Holding (Apollo's annuities arm), Johnson & Johnson Services, T-Mobile, Bloom Energy, and the American Petroleum Institute on TAX/FIN topics. Sullivan alone has appeared in 1,714 federal lobbying filings and lifetime-tracked revenue exceeding $76 million per OpenSecrets. The detector identified 16 named lobbyists representing $122 million in 2024-2026 lobbying income on topics directly aligned with the committee they previously staffed. **Bill-citation analysis confirms Brownstein Hyatt cited H.R. 1 (the 2025 'Big Beautiful Bill' tax-and-spending reconciliation) 256 times across its lobbying activities, and H.R. 5376 (Inflation Reduction Act) 37 times — the most-lobbied bills in the corpus by this single firm. Cross-corpus 'say vs. pay' signal: Sen. Elizabeth Warren issued ten 2024-2025 press releases publicly attacking Apollo Global Management over the Steward Health Care bankruptcy — while Sullivan + Warren billed the same Apollo $8.92M for representation during the same period.**

external_sources.purpose: Sullivan official firm bio — confirms Staff Director, Senate Finance Committee
OpenSecrets revolving-door record — career-tracked revenue figures
Warren biography — confirms Senate Finance / Ways & Means / Treasury history

limitations: Revolving-door + topic-match alone is not illegal. The finding documents a structural pattern; per-individual ethical or legal review is out of scope.
D11 keyword-mapping from covered_position text to former-committee is heuristic. Future iterations should use Congress.gov / LegiStorm staff databases for precise role-to-committee mapping.

Per LegiStorm (confirmed by the adversarial fact-checker), Mark Warren LEFT Brownstein for Capitol Tax Partners in May 2026 — i.e. during the publication window. The finding's present-tense 'Sullivan + Warren co-lobby Apollo' is accurate through Q1 2026 (the LDA window of our index) but should be qualified in any published copy as 'through Q1 2026'. Sullivan remains at Brownstein. The Apollo engagement may continue under Sullivan alone.

Specific revenue figures ($8.92M Apollo, $4.54M Athene, $1.65M T-Mobile etc.) are aggregated from our LDA index. Client relationships are confirmed via OpenSecrets (Sullivan's 2025 client roster explicitly includes Apollo, Bloom Energy, American Tower, Centene, API). Dollar specifics are internally computed and not separately reproduced from third-party aggregators.

POST-PUBLICATION UPDATE from OS-006 spotlight-handoff (May 22, 2026, three weeks after Warren's May 4 2026 announcement at Capitol Tax Partners): Apollo Global Management has STAYED with Russell Sullivan at Brownstein Hyatt. The Senate LDA database shows ZERO filings of any kind (registration, amendment, or quarterly) in which Capitol Tax Partners appears as registrant for Apollo. The Brownstein-Apollo engagement remains intact at $260K/quarter and the BHFS Q1 2026 filing (posted April 17, 2026) lists Sullivan as the lead tax-issue lobbyist with Harold Hancock. The Q2 2026 LDA filing deadline of July 20, 2026 is the definitive test of whether Apollo will migrate. Brownstein has already taken Warren's bio page to 404; Capitol Tax has not yet added Warren to its team page despite the May 4 announcement banner — an asymmetric public-presence picture indicating a fast departure but a slow practice integration on the receiving end.

C-005.statement: The Federal Election Commission has formally taken regulatory action against Christina Loren Clement's Senate campaign committee on the same fictitious-filing pattern data-detective surfaced from the LDA database. On April 28, 2026, the FEC issued a warning letter to her committee (STATE OF LOC NATION FOR CLEMENT FOR SENATE, FEC ID C00857128) over her $50.25 million reported self-loan; the FEC subsequently reclassified the filing into its 'False and Fictitious Filings' miscellaneous repository on the committee's public page. The 'loan' is not cash — Clement's own published policy states the $50.25M is the asserted fair-market value of a license to her self-issued 'Loc Nation Dollar' (LND) currency pegged at 1 LND = $750 USD. The pattern is not unique to Clement: Rico Cortez Dukes (b. 1979, Shreveport LA), the operator of the second sovereign-citizen-pattern LDA filing data-detective surfaced (THEYFEARTRUTH FEDERAL GOVERNMENT OF AMERICA), has a documented federal-court litigation history of at least eleven pro se complaints in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas (2017-2021), including textbook sovereign-citizen-style titles like 'Dukes v. Roman Empire' (3:17-cv-02834), 'Dukes v. Federal Reserve Central Bank' (3:17-cv-02510), and 'Dukes v. Trump' (3:17-cv-02167). Both Clement and Dukes are formally registered FEC 2024 presidential candidates of self-styled sovereign-government parties (Clement: FEC P40016412 REPUBLICAN PARTY; Dukes: FEC P00011163 AMERICAN INDEPENDENT PARTY, statement of candidacy filed 08/17/2021; THEYFEARTRUTH PRESIDENTIAL COMMITTEE C00884064).

C-006.statement: Akin Gump Strauss Hauer & Feld's complete 2025 FARA foreign-principal list is six sovereigns (UAE, Cambodia, Japan, Palau, Marshall Islands, Costa Rica) plus the Korea Embassy (March 2026 Exhibit AB). NONE of the four LDA-flagged Akin Gump engagements data-detective C-003/D10 surfaced — Ant Group Co. (CN), TP-Link Systems (SG/VG/GB), Adani North America (IN), United Solar Polysilicon (CN/OM) — are covered at firm OR attorney level FARA. The same partners (Pomper, Babin, Ros-Lehtinen, Kho) handle both sides but FARA-register only the government clients. The Adani engagement is the strongest 'gap should not exist' case: Akin Gump was retained THE DAY AFTER the November 20, 2024 DOJ Eastern District of New York indictment of Gautam and Sagar Adani; the lobbying targets are White House + State Department + Commerce Department on bilateral 'U.S.-India renewable energy cooperation'; the LDA-named foreign entity of interest is Adani Enterprises Limited — the indicted parent corporation. NYT reporting on May 18, 2026 indicates the DOJ is moving to drop the criminal case. The United Solar Polysilicon engagement is structurally adjacent to active US sanctions enforcement: the client's chairman/founder Zhang Longgen was CEO of Daqo (2018-2023) and vice-chair of Xinjiang Daqo, an entity on the BIS Entity List since June 2021 for Uyghur forced labor; the US Treasury voted AGAINST the IFC's $250M loan to this exact entity on August 8, 2025; Akin Gump's specific lobbying issue is the Section 232 polysilicon investigation. The TP-Link engagement uses Steve Kho — former Acting Chief Counsel for China Enforcement at USTR — to lobby on a potential ITC Section 337 exclusion for a router maker under active Commerce Department national-security review.

C-007.statement: Tarplin, Downs & Young LLC — a healthcare-policy lobby boutique surfaced by D11 — is the institutional home of two named Medicare Part D legislative architects who became drug-industry lobbyists. ProPublica's 2009 investigation 'Medicare Drug Plan Architects Now Drug Company Lobbyists' named TDY co-founders **Raissa Downs** (HHS Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary for Legislation; helped spearhead Part D implementation) and **Jennifer Young** (HHS Assistant Secretary for Legislation; Senior Counselor to HHS Secretary Mike Leavitt). The firm has held a pharma-heavy client roster — Amgen, AstraZeneca, BIO, Boston Scientific, Genzyme, PhRMA, Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Blue Cross Blue Shield — continuously for sixteen years and counting. **The strongest current say-vs-pay configuration**: TDY's $6M+ client **Vertex Pharmaceuticals is in active federal litigation against HHS-OIG** to set aside the agency's Anti-Kickback Statute interpretation of its Casgevy fertility-preservation program (Bass Berry & Sims / Law360, July 2024) — meaning a top-five TDY client is suing the precise federal agency (HHS-OIG) where two of TDY's three founders ran the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Legislation. The firm was acquired by FGS Global on September 10, 2025 — a market-structure event explaining the Q4 2025 spending spike data-detective's D1 detector flagged.

C-008.statement: **Reynolds American — parent of RAI Services Company, the $3.18M lobbying client of Ballard Partners' Daniel McFaul — paid Make America Great Again Inc. $5 million on April 30, 2026; Reynolds executives met Donald Trump in Jupiter, Florida two days later (May 2); and the FDA reversed its flavored-vape ban within approximately ten days.** The New York Times's Kenneth Vogel and Christine Jewett reported the timeline, corroborated across four independent secondary sources. McFaul is the lobbyist of record on RAI Services LDA filings; he is also Managing Partner of Ballard Partners' DC office, served on the 2016-17 Trump Presidential Transition Team in the Appointments office covering DoD, VA, Armed Services, and Intelligence, and served on Matt Gaetz's own congressional transition team. McFaul's personal FEC giving (46 contributions, ~$33K, 2017-2026, all Republican) explicitly includes Friends of Matt Gaetz (2018), Trump Victory + Trump for President (February 2020), and Brian Jack (former Trump WH Political Director, 2024). Ballard Partners' lobbying revenue grew 4.5× from $19.6M in 2024 to $88.3M in 2025 — making it the #1 lobbying firm in America by revenue — with current White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles and current Attorney General Pam Bondi as Ballard alumni.

C-009.statement: **Anthony 'Lazer' Lazarski at Cornerstone Government Affairs** — a 25-year USAF Colonel; former Senate Armed Services Committee Professional Staff Member; former Senior Legislative Advisor to SASC Chair Jim Inhofe — is the named lobbyist on Cornerstone's 2024 contracts with **Apollo Global Management, Boeing, General Dynamics, and Anduril**. He is attacked on the record by **Sen. Elizabeth Warren — a current SASC member** — on two independent axes simultaneously: (a) Warren co-signed a 2024 Senate letter naming Apollo by name and demanding accountability for Apollo's 'shadowy' role in the Steward Health Care bankruptcy; (b) Warren published a campaign platform — 'Reduce Corporate Influence at the Pentagon' — that verbatim describes Lazarski's exact revolving-door pattern ('giant contractors have deployed an extremely profitable strategy: recruit armies of lobbyists from former Pentagon officials and congressional staffers...My plan would ban giant defense contractors from hiring senior DOD officials and general and flag officers for four years after they leave the Department'). Lazarski's $108,400 in 2024 FEC donations went exclusively to SASC + HASC Republicans (Britt, Fischer, Mike Rogers, Sheehy, Lamborn, Kiggans, Gallagher) — a clean money-axis contrast with Warren's attack. **This finding triangulates C-004**: the same Apollo Global Management client is lobbied by TWO different mega-firms (Brownstein/Sullivan on Senate Finance committee jurisdiction + Cornerstone/Lazarski on Senate Armed Services jurisdiction), each via former senior committee staff, and the same senator — Warren — attacks Apollo from both committee positions.
